reviews.title: Scammy and Shady-Stay Away
reviews.text: I normally don’t write reviews but this one got me. I signed up then realized they want money to read messages…. Ok fine so I paid up and was attempting to locate a place to stay, normal pleasantries with the person seeking to rent. Our timelines didn’t match up, no worries right? Wrong they banned my account without notice of any kind, I just couldn’t log in. I could however talk to their chat bot, that was fun… it just kept saying “I understand why you want a clear reason. The exact reason for a specific account isn’t always shared. Accounts can be deactivated if activity breaks our community standards, such as:  Our terms also allow us to deny or remove access to the service at our discretion, even without a specific reason. If you believe the deactivation happened by mistake, you can explain the situation through the support chat on the login or signup screen and request a review.” Ok this is fun, they feel like this indemnifies them from any recourse. Smh. When I requested the review they said they would get back to me in less than 3 hours, didn’t happen. For the cost of a single week which was obnoxious they should jump through hoops to help CUSTOMERS, they don’t. This was all in a matter of 24 hours..  I’d rather dip my hand in hot oil than deal with them ever again. It’s all scammy. To clarify I am a homeowner, raised 4 kids, been at my job for over 20 years and I’m just looking for a place to sleep when I take an out of state position. Seems like a bad business pract

reviews.title: Beware of this APP, they don’t even deserve a 1 star
reviews.text:
I strongly advise everyone to be cautious with this app! I registered online but never actually used the platform, and the app isn’t even downloaded on my phone. Yet, I discovered that I had been charged weekly without realizing I was enrolled in a recurring subscription.

When I contacted customer support to dispute these charges and request a refund, the experience was even more frustrating. A representative named Janice was extremely unhelpful, dismissive, and inconsiderate of my concerns. Instead of offering a reasonable solution, I was left feeling completely disregarded as a customer.

I never knowingly agreed to these recurring charges, and I find their billing practices misleading and unacceptable.

BEWARE before entering your payment information! Check your subscriptions and payment history carefully. Based on my experience, I would not recommend Roomster. I am extremely disappointed with both their billing practices and customer service.

reviews.title: Overzealous Account Deletion
reviews.text: Both me and my tenant prospect had our accounts removed for “suspicious activity” when literally all we did was reach out to relevant landlords and tenants. This destructive over zealous approach to mass account deletion serves no purpose and is extremely reckless and unthoughtful, felt like I flushed my money down the toilet. And did they provide any explanation for what my “suspicious activity” was? No, they simply deleted my account without reason. Unacceptable and unprofessional.

reviews.title: Do Not Sogn Up! As Close to a Scam as it Gets!
reviews.text:
At first glance, it appears that there are numerous listings that match your criteria in the city we’re finding places is exceedingly difficult. After messaging several postings, I started receiving emails that I had new messages.

When I go to click on messages, the pay wall starts. $15 for seven days $30 for 30 days or $50 for 60 days. Then looking through my emails, I realized that none of the places I had reached out to you or messaging me back..

So you’re telling me that there’s people trying to rent a room, searching through these apps to find a potential roommate and ignoring all their messages, paying a ridiculous amount of money to message us to see if we want to rent a room from them?

No, I think not. It is a scam. They’re trying to get you to pay to see the messages and the messages will lead you nowhere. Do not sign up.

Edit: I’m providing a reply to the developer’s response to my review. I work in technology and manage bot-defense tools. False positives occur all the time, so blocks aren’t always for valid reasons. The callout here was that contact customer service about it was impossible because the verification process put me in a loop. Also, as it’s been several weeks since originally encountering the issue and sharing this review, I’ve since found a roommate on a competitor platform and don’t need this issue fixed for myself anymore anyway.

reviews.title: Paid subscription wasn’t worth it
reviews.text:
I decided to try Roomster and paid for a subscription, but unfortunately it wasn’t a great experience for me. I don’t live in a rural or desolate area, but I’m also not in a major downtown, and there were very few listings available.

I created a post and only received one response, which seemed like a scam. I ended up paying just to view it, and it felt like a waste. For the price, I expected more access, especially the ability to browse all listings instead of being limited to “matches for you.”

I can see how this app might work better in larger, more populated cities, but in my area it didn’t deliver much value. Personally, I regret purchasing the subscription and will be sticking with Facebook groups going forward since they’ve been more active and reliable for me.

reviews.title: Major room for improvements
reviews.text:
The design is mediocre, and the app is often glitchy. The so-called 24/7 customer support is just an AI bot that seems to know very little about the app itself or how to resolve even basic issues.

The listing setup process is also problematic. Many of the questions are vague and poorly worded, and at least two appear to be illegal to ask or answer in New York City. That raises serious concerns about how carefully this service was built and reviewed.

Overall, too much about the app and the way the service is structured feels half-baked, shoddy, and prone to errors. More than anything, the experience serves as a strong deterrent against paying for the pro version.

reviews.title: Spammers Area, Expensive Subscription, Low Value
reviews.text:
Roomster was a very disappointing experience. As someone genuinely looking for a room, I had to pay for an expensive subscription just to message people. Only after subscribing did I realize that the people posting rooms also need to have a paid subscription in order to reply. This is not clearly explained upfront.

Because of this setup, most conversations lead nowhere. On top of that, I received many spam and suspicious messages, which made the platform feel unsafe and unreliable. Instead of helping me find accommodation, it wasted my time and money.

Overall, Roomster is overpriced, poorly designed for real users, and filled with spammers. I would not recommend it to anyone seriously looking for housing.

The app seems decent at first until you realize that they force you to pay a ridiculous subscription fee just to be able to view messages. When someone messages you, you can’t view the messages unless you pay $12 per week and when you send messages to other people the reply rates are very low because very few people are going to pay that. I paid the $12 so I can view messages and they deleted my account 2 days later because I tried sending out my number and they don’t want anyone sending out their number “to avoid scams” but the only scam is that they want everyone paying $12 per week to use their stupid ripoff of an app. Just stick to Facebook or PadSplit and don’t waste your time or money.

reviews.title: Scam, Glitches
reviews.text: App seems like fraud, maybe app has been corrupted. Very glitchy. Initially tried to start an account to post a room for rent and it constantly bumped me into looking for a room. Then it allowed me to set up an account to post a listing and when I received a message from someone interested I needed their subscription to view it. Once I started my subscription and was able to view the messages, it was from people telling me they had a room available for rent. When I checked my account it was again set to looking for a room instead of listing one. I again started to post a listing of my room entering all of my information address and photos. Once completed it would not move to the next page. I tried this over and over again. Finally I logged out and went to log in and it said my account had been deactivated. When I messaged support they said it was for suspicious activity and they wanted me to send them a photo ID to verify. Needless to say, I canceled my subscription and deleted the app.

reviews.title: I have to PAY to message people?
reviews.text: I’ve literally had the app for an hour and just realized this, and it is totally ridiculous. And it’s not exactly a cheap subscription either. $30 a month just to MESSAGE people? Bffr. Not to mention, any numbers you put in the descriptions of a listing magically disappear. Ie. “A 6 month lease is $1,500.” Turns into, “A  month lease is  .” And every single account for potential tenants had the exact same description, which leads me to believe the rest of the 1-star reviews of this app with talk of bots and scams, is true. And all of the halfway sorry, or just straight up rude responses to other 1-star reviews, is also, ridiculous. Sounds like this app/company needs a completely new management and development team, immediately. Deleted almost immediately.

reviews.title: A total scam
reviews.text: The app doesn’t work, you’ll get inundated of messages from people looking for a room in counties different from the one you listed. Inexistent customer service. No response, no refunds. Do NOT BUY

reviews.title: Scammy & Buggy
reviews.text:
This app feels like it should still be in development. There are major issues. When you submit an announcement it doesn’t give you a confirmation, so every time you press the button it makes another announcement. Also the announcements go straight to people’s inbox? It just privately messages everyone in your area that you’re looking for a roommate or room. There are bugs when trying to update your personal information, specifically the description about you. It makes a toast about something going wrong. 

Never mind these issues, there’s not enough people using this to make it worth finding people. Also, you have to pay regardless, because you cannot message people to meet up or plan unless you BOTH have the payed subscription. It simply won’t allow you to message unless you pay. 

The cost per week is steep considering nobody is active and you can only chat with people if you both pay. It feels scammy as there’s an ID verification spot and a credit check option. I would not use this app. Use another service

reviews.title: Unauthorized Transactions
reviews.text:
I use the app for a month and deleted my account only to find I would be charged every single month after for an account that no longer existed or had access to when messaging customer service. They told me to cancel it through my Apple ID, which the subscription did not show up through there in order to respond to customer service you had to pay for a subscription… I told them I was gonna dispute the charge with my bank and then they said that they canceled my subscription for me a “ partial” refund.

If you want a mediocre app to have unauthorized charges to your card and to have a mediocre customer support reach out to you and barely fix your problem. Look no further.
